original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.

actual_scope: Prove that under the square condition P_s Z P_f = 0 the own-leaf degree-1 core-to-leaf block of the every-stage paired-star gap has rank at most rank(Z) for every half width q, show the constant 1 is attained, and deduce total thin rank at least 2 q ceil(g/3) on that schedule under the cited schedule analysis.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a changed query demand or caller. This package changes neither. It answers open question 1 of unpaidmoon's open PR #7050, a rank question about one fixed schedule family of the paired-star contract, and builds no word.
bottleneck_link: Side result. It raises a lower bound on total thin rank for one schedule family of the paired-star contract, which restricts where a g=31, q=26 endpoint could be sought. It does not price a supplier or change the signed moment.
stop_rule: Stop at the first verified factor-1 proof and its immediate consequence on the every-stage schedule. Leave leaf-to-core blocks, attainment and nested or crossed intervals open.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the rank lemma for complementary idempotents over any field, the factor-1 block bound with a sharpness witness at every q, and the conditional bound 2 q ceil(g/3). verify.py exhausts the q=1 domain over F_2, runs seeded random cases at q=2,3,4 and over F_2, F_3, F_5, F_7, recomputes the contributor sets for g up to 64, and runs rejection controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Do the leaf-to-core blocks of an every-stage word raise the total thin rank bound above 2 q ceil(g/3)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The core-to-leaf rank inequalities admit a covering point of value 2 q ceil(g/3), so any higher bound on this schedule needs the other side of the endpoint.
open_questions.first_step: Write the leaf-to-core degree-1 block of one internal gap under P_s Z P_f = 0 and test whether a map meeting leaves t-1, t, t+1 at full rank can also cancel its own leaf-to-core monomials.
open_questions.blocked_by: The leaf-to-core monomial comparison for internal gaps is not derived here or in the source note.

open_questions.question: Is total thin rank 2 q ceil(g/3) compatible with every core-to-leaf monomial of the endpoint at g=3, q=1, where the bound is 2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The bound is not shown to be attained. The only recorded control word at g=3, q=1 has total rank 6.
open_questions.first_step: Run an exhaustive census of one internal map of rank at most 2 in stage 1 against every core-to-leaf monomial, not only M_j.
open_questions.blocked_by: The full list of monomials that must cancel is not enumerated in this package.

open_questions.question: Does the block-triangular rank argument extend to nested or crossed stage intervals?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those schedules are outside the hypothesis, and no bound proved here applies to them.
open_questions.first_step: Derive the squared-monomial condition for one nested pair of stages, where the internal map is conjugated by another stage's half.
open_questions.blocked_by: The square condition changes when a full call of another stage stands between the halves.
